title: NUPL: 276 arrested ASEAN Summit protesters, journalists file motion for release
summary: A lawyers' group on Wednesday said they filed a motion before the Muntinlupa City prosecutor seeking the immediate release of 276 protesters and journalists arrested during a protest amid the opening…

blocks.text: A lawyers' group on Wednesday said they filed a motion before the Muntinlupa City prosecutor seeking the immediate release of 276 protesters and journalists arrested during a protest amid the opening of the ASEAN Summit 2026.
In a motion filed Tuesday, the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers (NUPL) has also asked for the dismissal of the complaints against the arrested individuals.
NUPL chairperson Edre Olalia confirmed the document to GMA News Online on Wednesday.
The lawyers argued that the continued detention of the respondents for more than 36 hours without the filing of charges before a court constituted a continuing violation of their fundamental rights.

They said the Philippine National Police (PNP), which filed the complaints against the arrested, failed to submit the required evidence within the period prescribed under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code.
The provision requires authorities to bring persons arrested without a warrant before the proper judicial authorities within 12, 18, or 36 hours, depending on the gravity of the offense.
As of the filing of the motion, the respondents had allegedly not received copies of the complaint-affidavits, witness affidavits, or other evidence.
Despite their continued detention, no information had been filed against them before any court, the lawyers said.
“No less than the 1987 Constitution provides that no person shall be deprived of liberty without due process of law,” the motion read.
NUPL also cited the respondents' right to a speedy disposition of cases, arguing that the inquest proceedings should not be used to justify prolonged detention beyond the periods allowed by law.

Also, NUPL questioned the legality of the arrests, saying many of the respondents were merely exercising their constitutional rights to free speech, peaceful assembly and to seek redress of grievances.
Earlier, the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) said that the arrested protesters are set to be transferred to a detention facility.
NCRPO chief Police Brigadier General Christopher Abrahano said authorities are waiting for commitment orders from the court.

“Finile na po natin ang kaso. Nakalagak na po sa prosecutor's office ‘yung kasong finile natin at pinoproseso na lang po ang pag-transfer sa detention facility,” he told GMA News’ Unang Balita in an interview.
(We have filed the case. The case has been filed with the prosecutor's office and the transfer to the detention facility is currently being processed.)
“Ngayon pa ay nandoon sa Camp Bagong Diwa 'yung ating mga naaresto at any time probably, makapag-issue na ng commitment order 'yung korte,” he said.
(The arrested protesters are still at Camp Bagong Diwa and any time probably, the court will issue a commitment order.) —VAL, GMA News
